story.conflict: A woman must decide whether her boyfriend's effort to avoid canceling can excuse secretly replacing himself with someone she was not dating.
story.hook: My boyfriend admitted paying his twin to go on three dates with me. One was the anniversary he said he'd never miss.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF SHOWING UP CANNOT BE OUTSOURCED
story.premise: A boyfriend admits paying his identical twin to attend three dates in his place, including the anniversary dinner he promised never to miss.
story.punchline: He could keep the souvenir of the dinner he hadn't come to.
story.script: I learned that when Alex's brother Dan asked him to settle what he owed for our anniversary dinner. Alex tried to laugh it off, then admitted he'd paid Dan to take his place on three evenings. They were identical twins, but I hadn't agreed to date both of them. I asked whether the dinner menu he'd framed for me was from an evening he'd missed. He said yes, but I'd had a good time. Dan said he'd needed the money and hadn't expected this to become a problem. I asked whether they'd planned to tell me. Alex said there was nothing to tell because it hadn't meant anything romantic to Dan. I said it had meant something to me. I'd spent that evening talking about my mother's operation, believing I was talking to my boyfriend. Alex said he'd been trying to keep his promise to show up while taking extra shifts. I asked why he hadn't called me and changed the plan. He said I'd been disappointed when he'd canceled before. So he'd let me trust a different person instead of letting me be disappointed with him. Dan apologized. Alex offered another anniversary dinner. I said I wasn't booking anything that evening. I went home alone and left the framed menu with him. He could keep the souvenir of the dinner he hadn't come to.
story.twist: The framed anniversary menu celebrates an evening the boyfriend did not attend, and the twin's financial need does not make either man's deception her choice.

youtube.description: She remembers a meaningful anniversary dinner. Her boyfriend has paid someone else to be the man she remembers sitting across from her.
youtube.title: The Anniversary Menu He Had Framed

story.conflict: An employee must decide whether to keep working when his employer treats restricted meal vouchers as wages while reserving actual money for the business.
story.hook: My boss paid me in vouchers for the restaurant where I worked. When I asked for cash, he said he had real bills to pay.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF REAL WORK DESERVES REAL PAY
story.premise: A restaurant owner pays an employee's wages in vouchers for the restaurant, then refuses to exchange them for cash because he has real bills to pay.
story.punchline: His vouchers hadn't been able to get me that far.
story.script: There should have been eight hundred dollars in my wage envelope. Gary handed me restaurant vouchers and said I could use them for meals whenever I wanted. I asked how I was supposed to pay my rent. He said I was getting the full value, and I could bring my family in too. I asked him to exchange the vouchers at the register, then. He said the cash there was needed for suppliers and the building rent. I said those were exactly the kinds of things I needed my wages for. He told me everyone had to help the business through a difficult week. Then he handed me next week's rota and said another full week would help us recover. I asked whether that week's wages would be cash. He said I shouldn't make everything about money. I put the rota back and told him I wasn't agreeing to another week for meal vouchers. He said I'd regret walking away from steady work. I still hadn't been paid for the week I'd finished. I called the temporary work agency I'd used before and asked about paid shifts. Two days later, I earned forty dollars helping unload a delivery. It wouldn't cover the rent on its own. But I bought a bus ticket home with it. His vouchers hadn't been able to get me that far.
story.twist: The owner's argument that his own bills require cash exposes why the vouchers cannot replace the employee's pay.

youtube.description: The owner says meal vouchers are worth the same as cash. His answer changes when the employee asks to exchange them at the register.
youtube.title: The Wage Envelope Full of Restaurant Vouchers

story.conflict: An athlete must decide whether keeping his team's sponsorship justifies surrendering an honest race result that his coach has already traded away.
story.hook: My coach promised the sponsor I'd let his son finish ahead of me. He wanted me to fake an injury to make it happen.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF AN HONEST RESULT STILL COUNTS
story.premise: A running coach promises a sponsor that his son will finish ahead of another athlete and asks that athlete to fake an injury.
story.script: He told me while handing out jackets with the sponsor's name on the back. I asked why I'd been included in the deal. Coach said the money kept our winter training sessions going, and I could give up one result for everyone else. Then he said I should pull out before the final so nobody needed to know. I asked whether the other runner had agreed to it. He said the boy's father handled that side. I found Ben warming up and asked him directly. He said he'd never asked me to pull out. He just wanted to race. When I went back, Coach said I'd embarrassed him and put the funding at risk. I said he was the one who'd promised a result before either of us ran. He told me not to expect him to keep coaching me if I couldn't put the team first. I needed those training sessions, and I hadn't suddenly found somebody else to coach me. I folded the new jacket on the bench and put on my old team vest. Then I lined up for the final. I finished fourth. Ben finished sixth. Neither of us won a medal. Coach wouldn't look at me afterward, and we still had to deal with what he'd promised Ben's father. But fourth place was mine. It wasn't the result he'd sold.
story.twist: The sponsor's son did not ask for the arrangement, and running honestly does not guarantee a medal or remove the coach's power to retaliate.

youtube.description: The new jackets come with a condition the athlete never agreed to. His coach expects him to give away his result for the team's funding.
youtube.title: The Sponsor's Name on the Team Jacket

story.conflict: A tenant must respond to a real intrusion when her landlord treats frightening her out of her home as a harmless trick.
story.hook: My landlord admitted dressing as a ghost to make me move out. The spare key in his hand worried me more than the sheet.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF THAT KEY WAS THE REAL PROBLEM
story.premise: A landlord admits dressing as a ghost and entering his tenant's flat at night to frighten her into moving out.
story.punchline: The problem had never been a ghost.
story.script: I found him by my kitchen after hearing someone moving inside at night. A white sheet was caught on his jacket, and his phone was ringing underneath it. Peter said I wasn't supposed to have seen him properly. I asked how he'd got in. He held up the key and said he was only having a bit of fun. He'd warned me that previous tenants thought the place was haunted. Now he admitted he'd been making the noises himself. I asked why. He said he'd promised the flat to someone who could move in next week, and I'd refused to leave before the date we'd agreed. He'd thought I might ask to go sooner if the place felt uncomfortable. I asked whether he understood what it had felt like to hear a person inside while I was trying to sleep. He said I was taking a silly joke too seriously. Then he asked whether this meant I was leaving after all. I told him staying somewhere else that night wasn't agreeing to his plan. I called my sister and asked whether I could come over. Before I went, I took a picture of him holding the sheet and the key and reported what had happened to the building manager. I slept at my sister's that night. The problem had never been a ghost.
story.twist: The supposed haunting is an attempt to make room for someone else, while revealing the disguise does not undo the fear caused by the landlord's access.

youtube.description: The tenant discovers who has been making noises in her flat. Removing the costume leaves a much more ordinary reason to be frightened.
youtube.title: The Spare Key Under the Ghost Costume
